title: Mikä: identifying or choosing one thing
summary: Use mikä to identify one countable thing or select one item. Mikä tämä on? — Tämä on kirja.
targetSkills: Mikä: identifying or choosing one thing
prerequisiteSkills: Ketkä: asking and answering about several people
objectives: Use mikä to identify or select one countable thing.
Name the thing or identify the selected item in a complete reply.

sections.title: Meaning and pattern
paragraphs: Singular refers to one person or one thing in these patterns.
An adjective is a word that describes a quality.
Use mikä to identify one countable thing or select one item. Mikä tämä on? (“What is this?”) asks for an identity; Mikä kirja on uusi? (“Which book is new?”) selects a book.
keyPoints: Mitä asks a different question about substance or classification; these examples identify or select one countable thing.

sections.title: Answering the question
paragraphs: Replace the missing identity or selection with the requested noun phrase. A single countable thing stays in the basic form: Tämä on kirja (“This is a book”). In a selection answer, give the distinguishing description: Tämä kirja on uusi (“This book is new”).
A natural short reply to “Mikä tämä on?” is “Kirja.” (“A book.”). Use the full reply when it makes the person, action or correction clearer.
A negative correction can reject a suggested identity before naming the actual countable thing. The complete negative phrase ei ole means is not.
The exercises show supporting Finnish words and their meanings when recalling them is not the task. Read the complete English meaning before choosing the question or answer form.
keyPoints: Keep the noun in its basic form when identifying one whole countable thing.
